# Claude Device Manager integration brief

You are adding Claude Device Manager (CDM) support to this app. CDM shares
Android/iOS devices between Claude Code sessions and other tools. This app
must take turns through CDM and must never touch a device it does not hold.
CDM is running right now on 127.0.0.1:{{PORT}}.

## Find the server
- Port: read ~/.claude-device-manager/port (trim whitespace). Host: 127.0.0.1.
  Do not hard-code {{PORT}}; the user can change it.
- No port file, or GET /cdm/ping not answering "cdm-ok": CDM is closed.
  Then run without locking. Never fail because CDM is absent.

## Holder ID
- Format "<app-name>:<slot>", e.g. "scrcpy-vwr:main". Stable across launches.
- Use one slot per concurrent device; a holder gets at most one Android
  and one iOS device.

## Acquire (blocking, streamed)
POST /cdm/acquire?holder=&category=&platform=&virtual=&device=&timeoutSec=
- category: phone | watch | tablet | phone,watch | any
- platform: android | ios (omit for either). virtual: true | false (omit for either)
- device: one specific device, by adb serial, hardware serial, iOS UDID or exact
  name (take "serial" from GET /cdm/devices). Waits in the queue for that device
  only. Category defaults to any. Unknown, ambiguous, don't-use, or ruled out by
  the other params: HTTP 400 with a one-line reason.
- timeoutSec: how long to wait in the queue (default 110).
- Read the body line by line, never buffered whole:
  "."                                  heartbeat every 5s, ignore
  "QUEUED <n>"                         queue position, show it to the user
  "GRANTED <platform> <id> <name...>"  id = adb serial or iOS UDID; name may have spaces
  "TIMEOUT <n>"                        re-call acquire to keep waiting
  "BLOCKED" | "REMOVED"                the user said no, stop and tell the user
- Closing the connection while queued leaves the queue. Use that for Cancel.

## Use
- Android: always pass "-s <id>" to adb/scrcpy. iOS: pass the UDID explicitly.
- Never: adb kill-server, adb -s <other>, simctl ... booted, simctl shutdown all.

## Keep the hold
- Holds are released after the idle time set in CDM (15 min by default).
  CDM cannot see this app's device commands, so while the device is in use
  call POST /cdm/renew?holder= (optionally &platform=) every 60s.
  It replies RENEWED, or NONE when the hold is gone.
- NONE, or no HOLDING line from GET /cdm/status?holder=, means the user took
  the device back: stop using it and re-acquire.

## Release
POST /cdm/release?holder=&platform=   replies RELEASED or NONE
- Call it on normal exit, window close, crash handler and shutdown hook.
- On startup, release once before acquiring, in case a previous run crashed.

## Observe (optional)
- GET /cdm/devices: JSON {devices:[{key,name,platform,category,virtual,online,
  dontUse,serial,holder:{id,label,agent}|null}], queue:[{position,holder,
  categories,platform,virtual,device}]}.
- GET /cdm/events: server-sent events; event "devices" carries the same JSON
  on every change.

## Done means
Every check passes against a running CDM:
1. CDM closed: the app starts and works without a lock, no error, no retry loop.
2. Two copies, one device: the second shows QUEUED 1 and gets the device after
   the first quits.
3. kill -9 while holding: on next launch it releases the old hold first.
4. Cancel while queued: GET /cdm/status for that holder returns NONE.
5. Release the device from the CDM window: the app notices within 60s.
6. Every adb or simctl call in the diff names the device.

If you are a Claude Code session testing this on a device yourself, you hold
a device through `cdm acquire` too. Give the app a different category or use
two devices, or the checks will deadlock.
